subject: psychiatry
title: Repetitive Behaviors in Autism and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder

steps.tx: **Echolalia** is the automatic, parrot-like repetition of vocalizations, words, or phrases spoken by another person, serving as a classic linguistic feature of autism spectrum disorder. Immediate echolalia involves repeating words instantly; delayed echolalia involves repeating commercial slogans or movie dialogues hours or days later.
steps.say: Echolalia is the parrot-like repetition of another person's speech, categorized as immediate repetition or delayed recitation of movie lines.

right.title: Delayed Echolalia (Scripting)
points: Recites dialogues or advertisements hours later
Highly characteristic of autism spectrum disorder

steps.tx: **Stereotypies and motor mannerisms** are repetitive, purposeless, rhythmic, coordinated motor movements exhibited by autistic children, including bilateral hand flapping, body rocking, toe walking, spinning objects, and finger flicking. These behaviors intensify during periods of emotional excitement, boredom, or sensory overload, functioning as sensory self-regulation.
steps.say: Stereotypies are rhythmic, purposeless movements like hand flapping or body rocking that increase with excitement or sensory overload.

vis.title: Repetitive Motor Phenotypes
rows: Rapid bilateral wrist and finger fluttering
Triggered by joy, excitement, or sensory overload
Sensory processing tactile defense or Achilles contracture
Sedative self-soothing in states of anxiety
Finger flicking in peripheral visual fields
Exploration of visual optical light refractions

steps.tx: This picture divides the diagnosis into the two groups of features that must both be present. **Autism spectrum disorder** requires persistent differences in social communication and interaction, together with restricted, repetitive patterns of behaviour, interests, or activities. Sensory sensitivities sit within the second group. Keeping the two domains separate helps clinicians check that an assessment has covered both halves of the criteria before reaching a conclusion.
steps.say: Diagnosis needs both halves shown here: social communication differences and repetitive, restricted patterns. Checking only one domain leaves the assessment incomplete.

vis.alt: Diagram of the two DSM-5 autism spectrum disorder symptom domains, covering social communication differences and repetitive behaviours
vis.caption: DSM-5 autism spectrum disorder symptom domains, showing reciprocal social interaction differences and repetitive behaviour patterns. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder**, abbreviated ADHD, is a persistent neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmentally inappropriate levels of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. Diagnostic criteria mandate symptom presence before age 12, persistence for at least six months, and impairment across two or more settings like school and home.
steps.say: ADHD features developmentally inappropriate inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity present before age twelve across school and domestic environments.

vis.title: ADHD Presentations
rows: Most common form; male predominance; school referral
More common in females; 'daydreamers'; missed early
Pre-school age children; squirming, running, climbing

steps.tx: **Neurobiology of ADHD** involves delayed maturation of prefrontal cortical networks, particularly the frontostriatal circuits connecting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex with the caudate nucleus and anterior cingulate gyrus. Neurotransmitter dysfunction features deficient dopaminergic and noradrenergic transmission, impairing the top-down cognitive gating of irrelevant sensory distractors.
steps.say: ADHD involves delayed maturation of prefrontal-striatal circuits and deficient dopamine and noradrenaline transmission, impairing attention gating.

nodes.label: Deficient prefrontal dopamine (D1) and noradrenaline (alpha-2A) signalling
Weakened prefrontal cortical inhibition over striatal motor output
Failure of executive working memory to filter extraneous stimuli
Clinical distractibility, motor restlessness, and behavioral impulsivity

steps.tx: **Methylphenidate** is the first-line psychostimulant medication of choice for ADHD, operating pharmacologically by blocking the presynaptic dopamine transporter (DAT) and noradrenaline transporter (NET). By increasing extracellular dopamine and noradrenaline in the prefrontal cortex, methylphenidate dramatically enhances attention span, task completion, and behavioral self-control.
steps.say: Methylphenidate blocks dopamine and noradrenaline reuptake in the prefrontal cortex, improving sustained concentration and executive focus.

right.title: Clinical Surveillance
points: Monitor blood pressure and resting pulse
Track appetite loss and growth deceleration
Utilize weekend drug holidays if growth slows

steps.tx: **Adverse effects of psychostimulants** include appetite suppression, abdominal pain, weight loss, delayed sleep onset insomnia, and modest transient deceleration in linear height velocity. Clinicians regularly monitor height and weight curves; implementing weekend or holiday 'drug holidays' allows catch-up physical growth without compromising school term academic learning.
steps.say: Stimulants can cause appetite loss, insomnia, and growth slowing. Monitoring growth charts and using weekend drug holidays preserves linear growth.

vis.title: Stimulant Side Effect Mitigation
rows: Skipping lunch at school; weight loss
High-calorie breakfast before dose; late evening snacks
Switch from extended-release to short-acting morning dose
Planned drug holidays during summer school vacations
Reduce dose or switch to non-stimulant atomoxetine

steps.tx: **Atomoxetine** is a non-stimulant medication approved for ADHD that operates as a highly selective inhibitor of the presynaptic noradrenaline transporter (NET). Because atomoxetine does not increase dopamine in the nucleus accumbens, it carries zero potential for substance abuse and represents the preferred agent in adolescents.
steps.say: Atomoxetine is a non-stimulant selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor. It carries no abuse liability and is ideal for patients with comorbid substance risk.

left.title: Atomoxetine (Non-Stimulant)
points: Takes 2 to 4 weeks for full therapeutic effect
Preferred in patients with substance risk or tics

right.title: Methylphenidate (Stimulant)
points: Controlled substance due to abuse liability
Dramatic immediate therapeutic effect on day one

steps.tx: **Behavioral classroom and parenting strategies** form an indispensable component of multimodal ADHD treatment, utilizing positive reinforcement, token economies, and structured visual organizers. Breaking complex assignments into small timed segments, sitting close to the teacher, and providing immediate feedback dramatically bolsters academic focus and social engagement alongside pharmacological stabilization.
steps.say: Parenting training and classroom accommodations like token economies and structured routines provide essential non-pharmacological support in ADHD.

nodes.label: Preferential seating: front row adjacent to teacher, away from windows
Chunking: break lengthy assignments into distinct 10-minute tasks
Token economy: immediate tangible rewards for completed tasks
Daily behavioral report card communicating between school and home
